hindi: अब इसलिए हम 'वेद की उत्पत्ति' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the origin of the Veda.

hindi: जैसा भगवान् धन्वन्तरि ने कहा।
english: As the Blessed Dhanvantari said.
notes: The sentence continues from unit 1 ('we shall explain, as the Blessed Dhanvantari said').

words.gloss: surrounded by the best of the gods and hosts of sages
Aupadhenava, Vaitaraṇa, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata, Karavīrya, Gopurarakṣita, Suśruta and others

hindi: तब आश्रम में विराजमान, देवश्रेष्ठों और ऋषिगणों से घिरे हुए, काशिराज दिवोदास भगवान् धन्वन्तरि से औपधेनव, वैतरण, औरभ्र, पौष्कलावत, करवीर्य, गोपुररक्षित, सुश्रुत आदि बोले।
english: Then Aupadhenava, Vaitaraṇa, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata, Karavīrya, Gopurarakṣita, Suśruta and the others said to the Blessed Dhanvantari, king of Kāśī, Divodāsa, who was dwelling in a hermitage, surrounded by the foremost of the gods and by hosts of sages.
notes: amara-vara-ṛṣi-gaṇa-parivṛtam: taken as 'surrounded by the best of the immortals and by hosts of sages'; amara-vara could also be read as one chief god, or the whole as 'excellent hosts of immortals and sages'. The name list is a compound ending in prabhṛti ('beginning with'); the names are taken as seven separate names. The edition's footnote on the name Karavīrya reads 'karavīra' (a variant name); the printed text is kept unchanged. Kāśirāja, Divodāsa and Dhanvantari are taken as appositives of one person.
lines_deva: अथ खलु भगवन्तममरवरमृषिगणपरिवृतमाश्रमस्थं काशिराजं दिवोदासं धन्वन्तरिमौपधेनववैतरणौरभ्रपौष्कलावतकरवीर्यगोपुररक्षितसुश्रुतप्रभृतय ऊचुः ॥

words.gloss: by bodily, mental and external diseases
afflicted by various pains and blows

words.gram: pres. part. vi-√ceṣṭ, m. acc. pl.
pres. part. vi-√kruś, m. acc. pl.
tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.
tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.
pass. part. upa-√diś, m. acc. sg.

hindi: हे भगवन्! शारीरिक, मानसिक और आगन्तुक रोगों से तथा नाना प्रकार की पीड़ाओं और आघातों से पीड़ित, रक्षक होते हुए भी अनाथों के समान छटपटाते और चिल्लाते हुए मनुष्यों को देखकर हमारे मन में पीड़ा उत्पन्न होती है। सुख चाहने वाले उन लोगों के रोग की शान्ति के लिए और अपने प्राणों के निर्वाह के लिए, एक हेतु से — इस पद का अर्थ संदिग्ध है — हम यहाँ उपदिष्ट होने वाले आयुर्वेद को सुनना चाहते हैं, जिसमें इस लोक और परलोक दोनों का कल्याण निर्भर है। इसलिए हम शिष्य के रूप में भगवान् के पास आए हैं।
english: O Blessed One, when we see men afflicted by diseases of the body, of the mind and of external origin, and by various pains and blows, who, though they have protectors, thrash about as if they had none and cry out, distress arises in our minds. For the cure of the disease of those who seek happiness, and for the support of our own lives, for a reason (pragāhita-hetoḥ; the sense of this phrase is doubtful), we wish to hear the Āyurveda that is taught here, on which welfare in this world and the next depends. Therefore we have come to the Blessed One as pupils.

text_flags.why: possible: ā+ā would normally coalesce to ā; the printed form leaves both (the editors mark atrā+āyattam). Read as atra āyattam.
possible: 'hetoḥ' is hard to construe; 'hetum' would make pragāhita-hetu an adjective of Āyurveda ('whose causes are thoroughly explored')

notes: pragāhita-hetoḥ is doubtful. As printed, it is read as a genitive/ablative of hetu with pragāhita ('plunged into, deeply considered'): 'for a deeply considered reason'. If hetum were read, the sense would be 'the Āyurveda whose causes are thoroughly explored'. Not applied to the text. atra āyattam: 'in it (Āyurveda) depends'. naḥ is taken as the genitive 'our'. teṣāṃ sukhaiṣiṇām refers to the men seen.
lines_deva: भगवन् शारीरमानसागन्तुव्याधिभिर्विविधवेदनाभिघातोपद्रुतान् सनाथानप्यनाथवद्विचेष्टमानान् विक्रोशतश्च मानवानभिसमीक्ष्य मनसि नः पीडा भवति तेषां सुखैषिणां रोगोपशमार्थमात्मनश्च प्राणयात्रार्थं प्रगाहितहेतोरायुर्वेदं श्रोतुमिच्छाम इहोपदिश्यमानं अत्राआयत्तमैहिकमामुष्मिकं च श्रेयः तद्भगवन्तमुपपन्नाः स्मः शिष्यत्वेनेति ॥
lines_iast: bhagavan śārīramānasāgantuvyādhibhirvividhavedanābhighātopadrutān sanāthānapyanāthavadviceṣṭamānān vikrośataśca mānavānabhisamīkṣya manasi naḥ pīḍā bhavati teṣāṃ sukhaiṣiṇāṃ rogopaśamārthamātmanaśca prāṇayātrārthaṃ pragāhitahetorāyurvedaṃ śrotumicchāma ihopadiśyamānaṃ atrāāyattamaihikamāmuṣmikaṃ ca śreyaḥ tadbhagavantamupapannāḥ smaḥ śiṣyatveneti ||

words.gram: gerundive adhi-√i caus., m. nom. pl.

hindi: भगवान् ने उनसे कहा, 'आप सबका स्वागत है। हे वत्सो, आप सभी परीक्षा करने योग्य नहीं हैं और पढ़ाने योग्य हैं।'
english: The Blessed One said to them: 'Welcome to you. All of you, dear children, are not to be tested and are to be taught.'
notes: amīmāṃsyāḥ: literally 'not to be examined/questioned' (here, as pupils not needing a test of fitness); the exact sense is interpretive.
lines_deva: तानुवाच भगवान् स्वागतं वः सर्व एवामीमांस्या अध्याप्याश्च भवन्तो वत्साः ॥
lines_iast: tānuvāca bhagavān svāgataṃ vaḥ sarva evāmīmāṃsyā adhyāpyāśca bhavanto vatsāḥ ||

words.gram: pa. part. pra-√nī, m. nom. sg.

hindi: यहाँ आयुर्वेद अथर्ववेद का उपांग है। स्वयंभू ने प्राणियों को उत्पन्न करने से पहले ही एक लाख श्लोक और एक हजार अध्याय बनाए; फिर मनुष्यों की अल्प आयु और अल्प बुद्धि को देखकर उसे पुनः आठ प्रकार से रचा।
english: Here, Āyurveda is a subsidiary limb of the Atharvaveda. Before producing beings, the Self-born (Brahmā) made it a hundred thousand verses and a thousand chapters; then, seeing the shortness of life and the smallness of intellect of men, he composed it again in eight parts.
notes: The object of kṛtavān and praṇītavān (Āyurveda) is understood. 'anutpādya eva prajāḥ' is read as 'without first having produced beings'.
lines_deva: इह खल्वायुर्वेदो नामोपाङ्गमथर्ववेदस्यानुत्पाद्यैवप्रजाः श्लोकशतसहस्रमध्यायसहस्रं च कृतवान् स्वयम्भूः ततोऽल्पायुष्ट्वमल्पमेधस्त्वं चालोक्य नराणां भूयोऽष्टधा प्रणीतवान् ॥
lines_iast: iha khalvāyurvedo nāmopāṅgamatharvavedasyānutpādyaivaprajāḥ ślokaśatasahasramadhyāyasahasraṃ ca kṛtavān svayambhūḥ tato'lpāyuṣṭvamalpamedhastvaṃ cālokya narāṇāṃ bhūyo'ṣṭadhā praṇītavān ||

hindi: वे ये हैं: शल्य, शालाक्य, कायचिकित्सा, भूतविद्या, कौमारभृत्य, अगदतन्त्र, रसायनतन्त्र और वाजीकरणतन्त्र।
english: They are: Śalya, Śālākya, Kāyacikitsā (treatment of the body), Bhūtavidyā (knowledge of spirits), Kaumārabhṛtya (rearing of children), Agadatantra (the doctrine of antidotes), Rasāyanatantra and Vājīkaraṇatantra.
notes: Names of the eight branches. Rasāyana and vājīkaraṇa are kept in Sanskrit; their scope is described in 8.7 and 8.8.
lines_deva: तद्यथा शल्यं शालाक्यं कायचिकित्सा भूतविद्या कौमारभृत्यं अगदतन्त्रं रसायनतन्त्रं वाजीकरणतन्त्रमिति ॥
lines_iast: tadyathā śalyaṃ śālākyaṃ kāyacikitsā bhūtavidyā kaumārabhṛtyaṃ agadatantraṃ rasāyanatantraṃ vājīkaraṇatantramiti ||

words.gloss: brief statement of the characteristics of each branch

hindi: अब इसके प्रत्येक अंग के लक्षणों का संक्षेप में कथन।
english: Now, a brief statement of the characteristics of each of its branches.

words.gram: dvandva + tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: उनमें शल्य वह है जो नाना प्रकार के तृण, काष्ठ, पत्थर, धूल, लोहा, मिट्टी के ढेले, अस्थि, बाल, नख, पीब, स्राव, दूषित व्रण और गर्भ के भीतर के शल्य को निकालने के लिए है, तथा यन्त्र, शस्त्र, क्षार और अग्नि के प्रयोग और व्रणों के निर्णय के लिए भी।
english: Among these, Śalya is for the removal of various kinds of grass, wood, stone, dust, metal, clods, bone, hair, nails, pus, discharge, vitiated wounds, and the śalya (dart) within the womb; and for the application of instruments, blades, caustic and fire, and the determination of wounds.
notes: The long compound is a list. duṣṭa-vraṇa and antar-garbha-śalya are taken as two items; duṣṭavraṇa could also be read with what follows (the removal of śalya from vitiated wounds). 'viniścaya' = ascertainment/determination. The final verb is understood: 'is for the sake of'.

words.gloss: resting in ear, eye, mouth, nose and so on

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: शालाक्य वह है जो गले की हँसली से ऊपर के भाग में स्थित, कान, आँख, मुख, नाक आदि में आश्रित रोगों की शान्ति के लिए है।
english: Śālākya is for the pacification of diseases located above the collar-bones, resting in the ears, eyes, mouth, nose and so on.
notes: jatru: the collar-bone region.

words.gloss: fever, rakta-pitta, wasting, madness, apasmāra, kuṣṭha, meha, atisāra and so on

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: कायचिकित्सा वह है जो सारे शरीर में आश्रित ज्वर, रक्तपित्त, शोष, उन्माद, अपस्मार, कुष्ठ, मेह, अतिसार आदि रोगों की शान्ति के लिए है।
english: Kāyacikitsā is for the pacification of diseases resting in the whole body, such as jvara (fever), rakta-pitta, śoṣa (wasting), unmāda (madness), apasmāra, kuṣṭha, meha, atisāra and the like.

text_flags.why: possible: long ī in the printed form; unit 7 and the sense give cikitsā

notes: Disease names are kept as the text's own categories, not modern diagnoses. The edition's footnote gives variant reading (O): atīsāra (not applied).

words.gloss: of those whose minds are seized by gods, asuras, gandharvas, yakṣas, rakṣas, ancestors, piśācas, nāgas, graha and so on
for pacifying the graha by propitiatory rites, offering of bali and so on
words.gram: dvandva + tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: भूतविद्या वह है जो देव, असुर, गन्धर्व, यक्ष, राक्षस, पितर, पिशाच, नाग, ग्रह आदि से ग्रस्त चित्त वालों के लिए शान्तिकर्म, बलिहरण आदि द्वारा ग्रहों की शान्ति के लिए है।
english: Bhūtavidyā is for those whose minds are seized by gods, asuras, gandharvas, yakṣas, rakṣases, ancestors, piśācas, nāgas, graha and the like, for the pacification of the graha by propitiatory rites, offering of bali and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: 'baloharaṇa' is not a known word; bali-haraṇa 'offering of bali' fits the sense

notes: graha = 'seizer' (a seizing spirit or influence); kept as graha. Gandharva, yakṣa, rakṣas, piśāca and nāga are classes of beings, kept as names.

words.gloss: for rearing children and purifying the faults of the nurse's milk
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

words.gloss: arising from vitiated breast-milk and graha

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: कौमारभृत्य वह है जो बालकों के पालन, धात्री के दूध के दोषों के शोधन के लिए है, तथा दूषित स्तन्य और ग्रहों से उत्पन्न रोगों की शान्ति के लिए भी।
english: Kaumārabhṛtya is for the rearing of children and the purification of faults in the wet-nurse's milk, and for the pacification of diseases arising from vitiated breast-milk and from graha.
lines_deva: कौमारभृत्यं नाम कुमारभरणधात्रीक्षीरदोषसंशोधनार्थं दुष्टस्तन्यग्रहसमुत्थानां च व्याधीनामुपशमनार्थम् ॥

words.gloss: for the signs of poison from bites of snakes, insects, spiders, rats and so on
words.gram: dvandva + tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

words.gloss: for pacifying combinations of various poisons
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: अगदतन्त्र वह है जो सर्प, कीट, मकड़ी, चूहे आदि के काटने से हुए विष के लक्षणों को बताने के लिए है, तथा नाना प्रकार के विषों के संयोग की शान्ति के लिए भी।
english: Agadatantra is for setting out the signs of poison from the bites of snakes, insects, spiders, rats and the like, and for the pacification of combinations of various poisons.

text_flags.why: possible: ś for ṣ in mūṣika (rat)

notes: vyañjana = 'manifestation, sign, characterisation'; the sense 'for stating the signs' is the literal rendering.

hindi: रसायनतन्त्र वह है जो वय को स्थिर रखने वाला, आयु, मेधा और बल को करने वाला तथा रोगों को दूर करने में समर्थ है।
english: Rasāyanatantra is that which keeps age steady, produces life, intellect and strength, and is able to remove disease.
notes: āyuḥ-medhā-bala-karam: 'making (increasing) life, intellect and strength'.

words.gloss: of those whose semen is scanty, vitiated, depleted or dried up
for the sake of producing nourishment, clarity and increase
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. as ind.
tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: वाजीकरणतन्त्र वह है जो अल्प, दूषित, क्षीण और सूखे हुए रेतस् वालों में पोषण, प्रसाद और वृद्धि उत्पन्न करने के लिए है, तथा अत्यन्त हर्ष उत्पन्न करने के लिए भी।
english: Vājīkaraṇatantra is for producing nourishment, clarity and increase in those whose semen (retas) is scanty, vitiated, depleted or dried up, and for producing great delight.
notes: nāmālpa...: 'nāma' and 'alpa-' run together. retas literally 'seed', here semen.

hindi: इस प्रकार यह आयुर्वेद आठ अंगों वाला बताया जाता है। इसमें किसे क्या कहा जाए?
english: Thus this Āyurveda is taught as having eight limbs. In this, to whom is what to be said?
notes: Spoken by Dhanvantari; 'atra' may also be taken as 'in this matter'.

hindi: वे बोले, 'हम सभी के लिए भगवान् शल्यज्ञान को मूल बनाकर उपदेश करें।'
english: They said: 'For all of us, may the Blessed One teach, making the knowledge of śalya the basis.'
lines_deva: त ऊचुः अस्माकं सर्वेषामेव शल्यज्ञानं मूलं कृत्वोपदिशतु भगवानिति ॥
lines_iast: ta ūcuḥ asmākaṃ sarveṣāmeva śalyajñānaṃ mūlaṃ kṛtvopadiśatu bhagavāniti ||

hindi: उसने कहा, 'ऐसा ही हो।'
english: He said: 'So be it.'

words.gram: pass. part. upa-√diś, n. acc. sg.

hindi: वे फिर भगवान् से बोले, 'हम एकमत वालों के मत को देखकर सुश्रुत भगवान् से पूछेंगे, और उसे जो उपदेश दिया जाएगा उसे हम भी धारण करेंगे।'
english: They said to the Blessed One again: 'Having regard to the view of us, who are of one mind, Suśruta will question the Blessed One, and we too shall take in what is taught to him.'
notes: 'bhūyo'pi' is taken with ūcuḥ ('again'). asmai is taken as dative 'to him' (Suśruta); upadhārayiṣyāmaḥ: 'we shall bear in mind/retain'.
lines_deva: त ऊचुर्भूयोऽपि भगवन्तम् अस्माकमेकमतीनां मतमभिसमीक्ष्य सुश्रुतो भगवन्तं प्रक्ष्यति अस्मै चोपदिश्यमानं वयमप्युपधारयिष्यामः ॥
lines_iast: ta ūcurbhūyo'pi bhagavantam asmākamekamatīnāṃ matamabhisamīkṣya suśruto bhagavantaṃ prakṣyati asmai copadiśyamānaṃ vayamapyupadhārayiṣyāmaḥ ||

hindi: उसने कहा, 'ऐसा ही हो।'
english: He said: 'So be it.'

hindi: हे वत्स सुश्रुत, यहाँ आयुर्वेद का प्रयोजन है रोग से पीड़ित लोगों को रोग से मुक्त करना और स्वस्थ की रक्षा करना।
english: Dear Suśruta, here the purpose of Āyurveda is the release from disease of those afflicted by disease, and the protection of the healthy.
lines_deva: वत्स सुश्रुत इह खल्वायुर्वेदप्रयोजनं व्याध्युपसृष्टानां व्याधिपरिमोकषः स्वस्थस्य रक्षणं च ॥
lines_iast: vatsa suśruta iha khalvāyurvedaprayojanaṃ vyādhyupasṛṣṭānāṃ vyādhiparimokaṣaḥ svasthasya rakṣaṇaṃ ca ||

hindi: इसमें आयु है, अथवा इसके द्वारा आयु को प्राप्त करता है, इसलिए यह आयुर्वेद है।
english: Life is found in this, or by means of this one finds life: therefore it is Āyurveda.
notes: A double etymology of āyurveda from √vid 'to be' (vidyate) and √vid 'to find' (vindati). 'vāāyur' keeps ā+ā uncoalesced in print.

words.gloss: by perception, tradition, inference and analogy

hindi: इसके श्रेष्ठ आदि अंग को, जो प्रत्यक्ष, आगम, अनुमान और उपमान से अविरुद्ध कहा जा रहा है, धारण करो।
english: Take in the foremost, first limb of it, which is being stated without contradiction from perception, tradition, inference and analogy.

text_flags.why: possible: short a in the second syllable; imperative of the causative upa-√dhṛ is upadhāraya

notes: 'aṅga-varam ādyam' could also be 'the first and best limb'.

words.gloss: from the healing of wounds caused by injury
from the joining of the head of the sacrifice
with a share of the sacrifice

hindi: यह अंग पहला है, पहले आघात से हुए व्रणों के भरने के कारण और यज्ञ के सिर को जोड़ने के कारण। क्योंकि सुना जाता है कि जब रुद्र ने यज्ञ का सिर काट दिया, तब देवता दोनों अश्विनों के पास जाकर बोले, 'हे भगवन्तो, आप दोनों हमारे सर्वश्रेष्ठ होंगे; आप दोनों द्वारा यज्ञ का सिर जोड़ा जाना चाहिए।' उन दोनों ने कहा, 'ऐसा ही हो।' तब उन दोनों के लिए देवताओं ने यज्ञ के भाग से इन्द्र को प्रसन्न किया, और उन दोनों ने यज्ञ का सिर जोड़ दिया।
english: Indeed this limb is the first, because of the earlier healing of wounds caused by injury and because of the joining of the head of the sacrifice. For it is heard that when the head of the sacrifice had been cut off by Rudra, the gods approached the two Aśvins and said: 'Blessed ones, you two will be our most excellent; the head of the sacrifice is to be joined by you.' The two said: 'So be it.' Then, for their sake, the gods propitiated Indra with a share of the sacrifice, and the head of the sacrifice was joined by the two.

text_flags.why: why: śeraḥ is not a word; sense and the parallel yajñasya śiraḥ elsewhere in the unit
possible: short a; bhāga 'share' is the usual word, though bhaga 'portion' would also fit

notes: prāg abhighāta-vraṇa-saṃrohāt: prāk is read as 'earlier' (the healing of wounds from injury being the earlier/primary matter); its exact function is uncertain and other readings are possible. The unit has a '|' mark after the first reason and after sandhātavyam iti; the printed line division here follows the source.
lines_deva: एतद्ध्यङ्गं प्रथमं प्रागभिघातव्रणसंरोहात् यज्ञशिरःसन्धानाच्च । श्रूयते हि यथा रुद्रेण यज्ञस्य शिरश्छिन्नमिति ततो देवा अश्विनावभिगम्योचुः भगवन्तौ नः श्रेष्ठतमौ युवां भविष्यथः भवद्भ्यां यज्ञस्यशेरः सन्धातव्यमिति ।
तावूचतुरेवमस्त्विति । अथ तयोरर्थे देवा इन्द्रं यज्ञभगेन प्रासादयन् । ताभ्यां यज्ञस्य शिरः संहितम् इति ॥
lines_iast: etaddhyaṅgaṃ prathamaṃ prāgabhighātavraṇasaṃrohāt yajñaśiraḥsandhānācca | śrūyate hi yathā rudreṇa yajñasya śiraśchinnamiti tato devā aśvināvabhigamyocuḥ bhagavantau naḥ śreṣṭhatamau yuvāṃ bhaviṣyathaḥ bhavadbhyāṃ yajñasyaśeraḥ sandhātavyamiti |
tāvūcaturevamastviti | atha tayorarthe devā indraṃ yajñabhagena prāsādayan | tābhyāṃ yajñasya śiraḥ saṃhitam iti ||

words.gloss: from the application of instruments, blades, caustic and fire
from being common to all branches

hindi: आयुर्वेद के आठों तन्त्रों में भी यही अधिक माना गया है, क्योंकि इसमें शीघ्र क्रिया की जाती है, यन्त्र, शस्त्र, क्षार और अग्नि का प्रयोग होता है, और यह सब तन्त्रों के लिए सामान्य है।
english: Among all eight branches of Āyurveda, this one alone is held to be foremost, because of quick action, because of the application of instruments, blades, caustic and fire, and because it is common to all branches.

text_flags.why: possible: extra 'mā' at the start; āśu-kriyā-karaṇāt is the expected reading and the only one that makes a clean list of three reasons

notes: Split follows the corrected reading. If 'āmā-' were kept, it would have to be 'āma' (raw/unripe), which does not fit the sentence. The first token is printed 'abhimataṃ' with anusvāra before the following word.

hindi: वह यह शाश्वत, पुण्यदायक, स्वर्ग की ओर ले जाने वाला, यशदायक, आयु के लिए हितकर और जीविका देने वाला है।
english: This is eternal, meritorious, conducive to heaven, to fame and to long life, and provides a livelihood.
notes: The subject (this Āyurveda, or the Śalya branch just discussed) is understood from context.
lines_deva: तदिदं शाश्वतं पुण्यं स्वर्ग्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं वृत्तिकरं चेति ॥
lines_iast: tadidaṃ śāśvataṃ puṇyaṃ svargyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ vṛttikaraṃ ceti ||

words.gloss: for the sake of the welfare of beings
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. gen. sg. as ind.

hindi: ब्रह्मा ने इसे कहा; उनसे प्रजापति ने पढ़ा; उनसे दोनों अश्विनों ने; दोनों अश्विनों से इन्द्र ने; इन्द्र से मैंने; किन्तु मेरे द्वारा यह यहाँ इच्छुकों को प्राणियों के हित के लिए दिया जाना चाहिए।
english: Brahmā declared it; from him Prajāpati learned it; from him the two Aśvins; from the two Aśvins, Indra; from Indra, I. But by me it is to be imparted here to those who seek it, for the welfare of beings.

text_flags.why: why: stray visarga; indrāt + aham gives indrād aham / indrādahaṃ

notes: Verbs and the object (this science) are understood in the lineage chain. adhijage is read as the perfect of adhi-√gā 'study' (alternatively adhi-√gam).
lines_deva: ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच ततः प्रजापतिरधिजगे तस्मादश्विनौ अश्विभ्यामिन्द्रः इन्द्रादःअं मया त्विह प्रदेयमर्थिभ्यः प्रजाहितहेतोः ॥
lines_iast: brahmā provāca tataḥ prajāpatiradhijage tasmādaśvinau aśvibhyāmindraḥ indrādaḥaṃ mayā tviha pradeyamarthibhyaḥ prajāhitahetoḥ ||

words.gloss: remover of old age, disease and death

lead_in_hindi: और इस विषय में यह श्लोक है।
lead_in_english: And in this regard there is this (verse).
hindi: मैं ही आदिदेव धन्वन्तरि हूँ, देवताओं के बुढ़ापे, रोग और मृत्यु को हरने वाला। मैं अन्य अंगों से युक्त शल्य-अंग का यहाँ फिर उपदेश देने के लिए पृथ्वी पर आया हूँ।
english: I am indeed Dhanvantari, the first god, remover of old age, disease and death for the immortals. I have come again to the earth to teach here the śalya branch, together with the other branches.
notes: 'amarāṇām' is read with the remover: 'for the gods'. 'gām' = earth (also 'cow'; earth fits the verb). Metre: four pādas of 11 syllables (upajāti/indravajrā type), consistent. The introductory 'bhavati cātra' is in lead_in.

words.gloss: union of beings made of the five great elements

hindi: इस शास्त्र में पाँच महाभूतों से बने प्राणियों के समवाय समूह को पुरुष कहा जाता है। उसी में क्रिया है; वह अधिष्ठान आधार है। क्यों? लोक की द्विविधता के कारण। क्योंकि लोक स्थावर और जंगम, दो प्रकार का है; और दो स्वभाव वाला ही है, आग्नेय और सौम्य; अथवा उन्हीं की अधिकता से पाँच तत्त्वों वाला है। उनमें प्राणि-समूह चार प्रकार का है, जिसके नाम संस्वेदज, जरायुज, अण्डज और उद्भिज्ज हैं। उनमें पुरुष प्रधान है; उसका उपकरण दूसरा अन्य है। इसलिए पुरुष अधिष्ठान है।
english: In this treatise the union of embodied beings made of the five great elements is called puruṣa. Action (kriyā) is in him; he is the substratum. Why? Because of the twofold nature of the world. For the world is twofold, stationary and moving; it is indeed twofold in nature, fiery (āgneya) and lunar (saumya); or, owing to the preponderance of those, it is of five natures. Among these, the multitude of beings is fourfold, named sweat-born, womb-born, egg-born and sprout-born. Among them the puruṣa is the chief; the other is his instrument. Therefore the puruṣa is the substratum.
notes: Syntax of 'tasmin kriyā so'dhiṣṭhānam' is terse; read as 'action is in him; he is the substratum' (kriyā left as 'action', not interpreted as treatment). 'tadbhūyastvāt pañcātmako vā' is ambiguous: 'tad' may point to the fiery and lunar natures or to the five great elements; translated literally. The class name here is saṃsvedaja; the next unit lists svedaja. 'kasmāt' opens an objection-style question answered by 'lokasya dvaividhyāt'. Single witness, no damaged words flagged.
lines_deva: तस्मिन् क्रिया सोऽधिष्ठानं कस्मात् लोकस्य द्वैविध्यात् लोको हि द्विविधः स्थावरो जङ्गमश्च द्विविधात्मक एवाग्नेयः सौम्यश्च तद्भूयस्त्वात् पञ्चात्मको वा तत्र चतुर्विधो भूतग्रामः संस्वेदजरायुजाण्डजोद्भिज्जसंज्ञः तत्र पुरुषः प्रधानं तस्योपकरणमन्यत् तस्मात् पुरुषोऽधिष्ठानम् ॥
lines_iast: tasmin kriyā so'dhiṣṭhānaṃ kasmāt lokasya dvaividhyāt loko hi dvividhaḥ sthāvaro jaṅgamaśca dvividhātmaka evāgneyaḥ saumyaśca tadbhūyastvāt pañcātmako vā tatra caturvidho bhūtagrāmaḥ saṃsvedajarāyujāṇḍajodbhijjasaṃjñaḥ tatra puruṣaḥ pradhānaṃ tasyopakaraṇamanyat tasmāt puruṣo'dhiṣṭhānam ||

hindi: उस पुरुष के दुःख से जो संयोग होते हैं, वे व्याधि कहलाते हैं।
english: The conjunctions with suffering of that (person) are called diseases (vyādhi).
notes: 'tad' is taken as the puruṣa of the previous unit; compound read as 'conjunction with his suffering'. Alternative: those (conditions) that are conjoined with suffering.

hindi: वे चार प्रकार के हैं: आगन्तुक, शारीरिक, मानसिक और स्वाभाविक।
english: They are fourfold: adventitious, bodily, mental and natural.
lines_deva: ते चतुर्विधाः आगन्तवः शारीराः मानसाः स्वाभाविकाश्चेति ॥
lines_iast: te caturvidhāḥ āgantavaḥ śārīrāḥ mānasāḥ svābhāvikāśceti ||

hindi: इनमें आगन्तुक रोग चोट आघात के कारण होते हैं।
english: Of these, the adventitious ones are caused by injury.

words.gloss: caused by imbalance of vāta, pitta, kapha, blood and their combination

hindi: शारीरिक रोग अन्न और पान भोजन-पेय से उत्पन्न होते हैं और वात, पित्त, कफ, रक्त तथा सन्निपात की विषमता के कारण होते हैं।
english: The bodily ones are rooted in food and drink, and are caused by imbalance of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood and their combination (sannipāta).
notes: 'sannipāta' may be read as a separate item (combination of the doṣas) or as part of a list of five; kept as a member and glossed 'combination'. 'vaiṣamya' = unevenness, imbalance.

words.gloss: anger, grief, fear, elation, despondency, jealousy, resentment, wretchedness, envy, desire, greed and the like
through the divisions of desire and aversion

hindi: मानसिक रोग क्रोध, शोक, भय, हर्ष, विषाद, ईर्ष्या, असूया, दैन्य, मात्सर्य, काम, लोभ आदि हैं; वे इच्छा और द्वेष के भेदों से होते हैं।
english: The mental ones — anger, grief, fear, elation, despondency, jealousy, resentment, wretchedness, envy, desire, greed and the like — arise through the divisions of desire and aversion.
notes: Translation of the emotion terms is the plain dictionary sense (īrṣyā jealousy, abhyasūyā resentment/spite, dainya wretchedness, mātsarya envy). 'bhavanti' may be read 'arise' or 'are'.

words.gloss: hunger, thirst, old age, death, sleep and the like

hindi: स्वाभाविक रोग भूख, प्यास, बुढ़ापा, मृत्यु, निद्रा आदि हैं।
english: The natural ones are hunger, thirst, old age, death, sleep and the like.
notes: Final member 'prakṛti' (nature, kind) is read in the sense 'and the like', as prabhṛti is used in the preceding unit; it could also be read 'having hunger ... as their nature'.

words.gloss: having mind and body as their seat

hindi: ये सब रोग मन और शरीर में स्थित होते हैं इनका अधिष्ठान मन और शरीर है।
english: These (diseases) have the mind and the body as their seat.

hindi: इन रोगों के निग्रह दमन के हेतु हैं: संशोधन, संशमन, आहार और आचार, जब वे ठीक प्रकार से प्रयुक्त किए जाएँ।
english: For these, purification (saṃśodhana), pacification (saṃśamana), diet and conduct, properly applied, are the means of checking them.

hindi: प्राणियों का मूल आहार है, और बल, वर्ण तथा ओज का भी; वह छह रसों पर आश्रित है। रस फिर द्रव्यों में आश्रित रहते हैं; द्रव्य फिर औषधियाँ हैं। वे औषधियाँ दो प्रकार की हैं: स्थावर और जंगम।
english: Food is the root of living beings, and of strength, complexion and ojas; it depends on the six tastes (rasa). The tastes in turn rest on substances (dravya); the substances in turn are oṣadhis (medicinal substances). These are twofold: stationary and moving.
notes: 'oṣadhi' is used here for medicinal substances in general (both stationary and moving), unlike its narrow sense in the next unit. 'rasa' = taste. 'tāḥ' agrees with oṣadhayaḥ (f.).
lines_deva: प्राणिनां पुनर्मूलमाहारो बलवर्णौजसां च स षट्सु रसेष्वायत्तः रसाः पुनर्द्रव्याश्रयाः द्रव्याणि पुनरोषधयः ।
lines_iast: prāṇināṃ punarmūlamāhāro balavarṇaujasāṃ ca sa ṣaṭsu raseṣvāyattaḥ rasāḥ punardravyāśrayāḥ dravyāṇi punaroṣadhayaḥ |

words.gloss: ending with the ripening of fruit

hindi: उनमें स्थावर चार प्रकार की हैं: वनस्पति, वृक्ष, वीरुध और ओषधि। उनमें जो बिना पुष्प के फल वाली हैं वे वनस्पति हैं; जो पुष्प और फल वाले हैं वे वृक्ष हैं; जो फैलने वाली लताओं वाली और झाड़ी गुल्म बनाने वाली हैं वे वीरुध हैं; और जिनका अन्त फल के पक जाने पर होता है वे ओषधि हैं।
english: Of these, the stationary ones are fourfold: vanaspati, vṛkṣa, vīrudh and oṣadhi. Among them, those that bear fruit without flowers are vanaspatis; those that bear flowers and fruit are vṛkṣas; those with spreading tendrils and those growing in clumps are vīrudhs; and those that end with the ripening of the fruit are oṣadhis.
notes: The four class names are kept in Sanskrit. 'pratānavatyaḥ stambinyaśca' read as two kinds of vīrudh (spreading-tendril and clump-forming); 'phalapākaniṣṭhāḥ' = whose end comes with the ripening of fruit. 'apuṣpāḥ phalavantaḥ' = fruiting without (visible) flowers, literal.
lines_deva: तासां स्थावराश्चतुर्विधाः वनस्पतयो वृक्षा वीरुध ओषधय इति ।
तासु अपुष्पाः फलवन्तो वनस्पतयः पुष्पफलवन्तो वृक्षाः प्रतानवत्यः स्तम्बिन्यश्च वीरुधः फलपाकनिष्ठा ओषधय इति ॥
lines_iast: tāsāṃ sthāvarāścaturvidhāḥ vanaspatayo vṛkṣā vīrudha oṣadhaya iti |
tāsu apuṣpāḥ phalavanto vanaspatayaḥ puṣpaphalavanto vṛkṣāḥ pratānavatyaḥ stambinyaśca vīrudhaḥ phalapākaniṣṭhā oṣadhaya iti ||

words.gloss: beasts, humans, beasts of prey and so on
birds, snakes, creeping creatures and so on
worms, insects, ants and so on

hindi: जंगम भी चार प्रकार के हैं: जरायुज, अण्डज, स्वेदज और उद्भिज्ज। उनमें पशु, मनुष्य, व्याल हिंस्र जन्तु आदि जरायुज हैं; पक्षी, सर्प, सरीसृप आदि अण्डज हैं; कृमि, कीट, चींटी आदि स्वेदज हैं; इन्द्रगोप, मेंढक आदि उद्भिज्ज हैं।
english: The moving ones, too, are fourfold: womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born and sprout-born. Among them, beasts, humans, beasts of prey and the like are womb-born; birds, snakes, creeping creatures and the like are egg-born; worms, insects, ants and the like are sweat-born; indragopas, frogs and the like are sprout-born.

text_flags.why: possible: r dropped; the sense requires 'fourfold' (caturvidha); the devanāgarī also reads चतुविधाः, and the same spelling recurs in 35

notes: 'vyāla' is taken as beast of prey (could also be snake); 'indragopa' is kept as a creature name, not identified. 'sarīsṛpa' = creeping creature, reptile.
lines_deva: तत्र पशुमनुष्यव्यालादयो जरायुजाः खगसर्पसरीसृपप्रभृतयोऽण्डजाः कृमिकीटपिपीलिकाप्रभृतयः स्वेदजाः इन्द्रगोपमण्डूकप्रभृतय उद्भिज्जाः ॥
lines_iast: tatra paśumanuṣyavyālādayo jarāyujāḥ khagasarpasarīsṛpaprabhṛtayo'ṇḍajāḥ kṛmikīṭapipīlikāprabhṛtayaḥ svedajāḥ indragopamaṇḍūkaprabhṛtaya udbhijjāḥ ||

words.gloss: bark, leaf, flower, fruit, root, bulb, exudate, expressed juice and so on
hide, nails, hair, blood and so on

hindi: उनमें स्थावरों से त्वचा छाल, पत्र, पुष्प, फल, मूल, कन्द, निर्यास गोंद, स्वरस आदि प्रयोजन वाले उपयोगी हैं; और जंगमों से चर्म, नख, रोम, रुधिर आदि।
english: Among these, from the stationary ones, bark, leaves, flowers, fruits, roots, bulbs, exudates, expressed juices and the like are useful; from the moving ones, hide, nails, hair, blood and the like.
notes: The verb is understood: 'jaṅgamebhyaḥ ... ādayaḥ' = 'from the moving ones, hide ... are useful'. 'tvak' = bark or skin; read as bark for plants.

words.gloss: gold, silver, gem, pearl, manaḥśilā, clay, potsherd and so on

hindi: पार्थिव पृथ्वी से उत्पन्न द्रव्य हैं: सुवर्ण, रजत, मणि, मुक्ता, मनःशिला, मिट्टी, कपाल खपरा आदि।
english: The earthy ones are gold, silver, gems, pearls, manaḥśilā, clay, potsherds and the like.
notes: 'manaḥśilā' is a mineral substance name, kept untranslated. 'mṛtkapāla' could be one item (earthen potsherd) or two (clay; potsherd); split into two.

words.gloss: windy and windless conditions, sunshine, shade, moonlight, darkness, cold, heat, rain, day-and-night, fortnight, month, season, half-year course and so on

hindi: कालकृत काल से बने द्रव्य हैं: प्रवात हवादार, निवात हवारहित, आतप धूप, छाया, ज्योत्स्ना चाँदनी, अन्धकार, शीत, उष्ण, वर्षा, अहोरात्र, पक्ष, मास, ऋतु, अयन आदि, जो संवत्सर वर्ष के भेद हैं।
english: The time-made ones are windy and windless conditions, sunshine, shade, moonlight, darkness, cold, heat, rain, day-and-night, fortnight, month, season, half-year course (ayana) and the like, being divisions of the year.
notes: 'varṣa' is read as rain (it could also be 'year', but 'saṃvatsara' follows). 'ayana' = the sun's northward or southward course (half-year). 'saṃvatsaraviśeṣāḥ' read as in apposition to the whole list.

words.gloss: causes of accumulation, aggravation, pacification and counteraction

hindi: ये सब स्वभाव से ही दोषों के संचय, प्रकोप, प्रशमन और प्रतीकार के हेतु हैं और प्रयोजन वाले उपयोगी हैं।
english: These, by their very nature, are causes of the accumulation, aggravation, pacification and counteraction of the doṣas, and are useful.
lines_deva: त एते स्वभावत एव दोषाणां सञ्चयप्रकोपप्रशमप्रतीकारहेतवः प्रयोजनवन्तश्च ॥
lines_iast: ta ete svabhāvata eva doṣāṇāṃ sañcayaprakopapraśamapratīkārahetavaḥ prayojanavantaśca ||

hindi: शारीरिक विकारों के प्रकोप और प्रशमन में यह चार प्रकार का वर्ग हेतु कारण कहा गया है, चिकित्सकों द्वारा।
english: Physicians have declared this fourfold group to be the cause, both in the aggravation and in the pacification of bodily disorders.

text_flags.why: possible: r dropped; 'fourfold' is caturvidha; the same spelling recurs in 30

notes: 'eṣa vargaḥ' refers to the fourfold group of stationary, moving, earthy and time-made things. Metre is regular (16 syllables) either way.

hindi: जो आगन्तुज रोग हैं, वे दो प्रकार से पड़ते हैं: कुछ मन में, दूसरे शरीर में; और उनकी चिकित्सा क्रिया दो प्रकार की है।
english: The adventitious diseases fall in two ways: some in the mind, others in the body; and the treatment of them is twofold.
notes: 'kriyā' rendered 'treatment' here in the context of rogas.
lines_deva: आगन्तवस्तु ये रोगास्ते द्विधा निपतन्ति हि ।
मनस्यन्ये शरीरेऽन्ये तेषां तु द्विविधा क्रिया ॥
lines_iast: āgantavastu ye rogāste dvidhā nipatanti hi |
manasyanye śarīre'nye teṣāṃ tu dvividhā kriyā ||

words.gloss: of those fallen in the body

hindi: शरीर में पड़े आगन्तुक रोगों का उपक्रम चिकित्सा शारीरिक रोगों के समान है; और मानसिक रोगों के लिए शब्द आदि का अभीष्ट वर्ग सुख देने वाला है।
english: For those fallen in the body the treatment is like that of the bodily ones; but for the mental ones, the desired group beginning with sound brings comfort.
notes: Second line has no verb; 'upakramaḥ' (treatment) is understood, and 'the means' is added to complete the sense. 'śabdādi' = sound and the other objects of the senses, taken literally as 'sound and the rest'.

words.gram: ppp. n. nom. sg. √khyā with vi-ā

words.gloss: group of substances from which it arises
skin, flesh, bone, vessels, ligaments and so on
caused by imbalance of vāta, pitta, kapha, blood and their combination
of substances, tastes, qualities, vīrya and vipāka

hindi: इस प्रकार पुरुष, व्याधि, औषध और क्रियाकाल, यह चतुष्टय संक्षेप से बताया गया। उसमें पुरुष के ग्रहण से जिनसे वह उत्पन्न होता है उन द्रव्यों का समूह, भूत आदि, कहा गया, और उसके अंग, प्रत्यंग तथा उनके विभाग, त्वचा, मांस, अस्थि, सिरा, स्नायु आदि भी। व्याधि के ग्रहण से वात, पित्त, कफ, रक्त और सन्निपात की विषमता से होने वाले सभी रोग बताए गए। ओषध के ग्रहण से द्रव्य, रस, गुण, वीर्य और विपाक का निर्देश है। क्रिया के ग्रहण से छेद्य आदि और स्नेह आदि कर्म बताए गए। काल के ग्रहण से सब क्रियाओं के कालों का निर्देश है।
english: Thus this fourfold set — puruṣa, disease, medicinal substance and time of action — has been explained in brief. Among these, by the mention of puruṣa, the group of substances from which he arises, beginning with the elements (bhūta), is stated, together with his limbs, sub-limbs and divisions: skin, flesh, bone, vessels (sirā), ligaments (snāyu) and so on. By the mention of disease, all diseases caused by imbalance of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood and their combination are explained. By the mention of oṣadha, the indication of substances, tastes, qualities, vīrya (potency) and vipāka (post-digestive change) is given. By the mention of kriyā, the procedures beginning with excision (chedya) and those beginning with oleation (sneha) are explained. By the mention of kāla, the indication of all the times of action is given.

text_flags.why: possible: n for m; 'flesh' is māṃsa (tvak + māṃsa gives tvaṅmāṃsa); the Devanāgarī also reads नांसा
possible: v for r; 'sava' has no sense here and 'all times of action' fits; the Devanāgarī reads सवक्रिया

notes: Both flagged readings are kept as printed; words contain the corrected forms. 'kriyākāla' is read as one item (time of action) in the first sentence, then 'kriyā' and 'kāla' are taken up separately in the lines that follow, which makes five mentions for a 'fourfold' set; noted, not resolved. 'chedyādīni snehādīni ca karmāṇi' could also be read 'operations such as the to-be-excised (chedya) kind and the oleation kind'; translated literally. Disease list here covers only the bodily causes listed in 25.2. vīrya = potency, vipāka = post-digestive change, glossed only.
lines_deva: एवमेतत् पुरुषो व्याधिरौषधं क्रियाकाल इति चतुष्टयं समासेन व्याख्यातम् ।

तत्र पुरुषग्रहणात्तत्संभवद्रव्यसमूहो भूतादिरुक्तस्तदङ्गप्रत्यङ्गविकल्पाश्च त्वङ्नांसास्थिसिरास्नायुप्रभृतयः व्याधिग्रहणाद्वातपित्तकफशोणितसन्निपातवैषम्यनिमित्ताः सर्व एव व्याधयो व्याख्याताः ओषधग्रहणाद्द्रव्यरसगुणवीर्यविपाकानामादेशः क्रियाग्रहणाच्छेद्यादीनि स्नेहादीनि च कर्माणि व्याख्यातानि कालग्रहणात् सवक्रियाकालानामादेशः ॥
lines_iast: evametat puruṣo vyādhirauṣadhaṃ kriyākāla iti catuṣṭayaṃ samāsena vyākhyātam |

tatra puruṣagrahaṇāttatsaṃbhavadravyasamūho bhūtādiruktastadaṅgapratyaṅgavikalpāśca tvaṅnāṃsāsthisirāsnāyuprabhṛtayaḥ vyādhigrahaṇādvātapittakaphaśoṇitasannipātavaiṣamyanimittāḥ sarva eva vyādhayo vyākhyātāḥ oṣadhagrahaṇāddravyarasaguṇavīryavipākānāmādeśaḥ kriyāgrahaṇācchedyādīni snehādīni ca karmāṇi vyākhyātāni kālagrahaṇāt savakriyākālānāmādeśaḥ ||

words.gram: ppp. n. nom. sg. √kīrt with pra

hindi: चिकित्सा का यह बीज संक्षेप से कहा गया है। इसकी व्याख्या एक सौ बीस अध्यायों में होगी।
english: This is the seed of therapeutics, proclaimed in brief. Its exposition will be in one hundred and twenty chapters.
notes: 'saviṃśam adhyāyaśatam' (a hundred chapters with twenty) is in apposition to 'vyākhyā'; 'in' is supplied in the translation.

words.gloss: in Sūtra, Nidāna, Śārīra, Cikitsita and Kalpa

hindi: और इन एक सौ बीस अध्यायों को विषय के अनुसार सूत्र, निदान, शारीर, चिकित्सित और कल्प, इन पाँच स्थानों में बाँटकर, शेष विषयों को हम उत्तर बाद के तन्त्र में समझाएँगे।
english: And having divided these one hundred and twenty chapters, according to subject matter, into five sections — Sūtra, Nidāna, Śārīra, Cikitsita and Kalpa — we shall explain the remaining topics in the later treatise.
notes: 'uttare tantre' is rendered 'in the later treatise'; the text states it as a locative phrase, not as a proper name. 'arthavaśāt' = by the force/requirement of the subject.
lines_deva: तच्च सविंशमध्यायशतं पञ्चसु स्थानेषु सूत्रनिदानशारीरचिकित्सितकल्पेष्वर्थवशात् संविभज्य उत्तरे तन्त्रे शेषानर्थान् व्याख्यास्यामः ॥
lines_iast: tacca saviṃśamadhyāyaśataṃ pañcasu sthāneṣu sūtranidānaśārīracikitsitakalpeṣvarthavaśāt saṃvibhajya uttare tantre śeṣānarthān vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||

words.gram: ppp. n. nom. sg. √vac with pra

words.gloss: made known by the lord of Kāśī
sharing of the world of Śakra (Indra)

hindi: स्वयम्भू द्वारा कहे गए, सनातन और काशीपति द्वारा प्रकाशित इस शास्त्र को जो पढ़ता है, वह पुण्यकर्मा, पृथ्वी पर राजाओं द्वारा पूजित होकर, प्राणों के क्षय मृत्यु के समय शक्र इन्द्र के साथ एक ही लोक की प्राप्ति करेगा।
english: Whoever reads this eternal (teaching), spoken by the Self-existent one and made known by the lord of Kāśī, being of meritorious deeds and honoured on earth by kings, would at the end of life attain the same world as Śakra (Indra).
notes: 'idam' is taken to refer to this treatise or its teaching; the verse names no noun. 'Kāśīpati' is the lord of Kāśī, not named in the verse. Metre: two lines of 24 syllables, regular (Vaṃśastha-like, 12+12). 'paṭhed dhi yaḥ ... sa' is a correlative sentence.
lines_deva: स्वयम्भुवा प्रोक्तमिदं सनातनं पठेद्धि यः काशिपतिप्रकाशितम् ।
स पुण्यकर्मा भुवि पूजितो नृपैरसुक्षये शक्रसलोकतां व्रजेत् ॥
lines_iast: svayambhuvā proktamidaṃ sanātanaṃ paṭheddhi yaḥ kāśipatiprakāśitam |
sa puṇyakarmā bhuvi pūjito nṛpairasukṣaye śakrasalokatāṃ vrajet ||
